author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dr. Selim Suner was at home in North Kingstown with his infant son on September 11, 2001, before events drew him to Rhode Island Hospital and then New York. As leader of the Rhode Island Disaster Medical Assistance Team, he helped mobilize a federal response unit for Ground Zero.

Suner told Ocean State Media that the team included physicians, nurses, paramedics and logistics specialists. Its members initially expected to treat people rescued from the World Trade Center, but New York hospitals had already received the survivors by the time the Rhode Island group arrived.

The mission shifted to caring for rescuers working amid smoke, debris and continuing fires. Suner said the team treated thousands of police officers, firefighters, military personnel, construction workers, search-and-rescue members and working dogs during long shifts at the site.

Now a Brown University physician, Suner reflected on the deployment for the 25th anniversary of the attacks. His account places Rhode Island’s medical-response network within the broader recovery effort and records how quickly local clinicians moved from routine work to a disaster operation hundreds of miles away.
dek: Dr. Selim Suner led a Rhode Island disaster team whose mission shifted from treating survivors to caring for first responders.
headline: Rhode Island doctor recalls medical deployment to Ground Zero
